info.title: Nex Controller and Core API
info.description: Implemented development API for administrator inventory, enrollment, durable operations, appliance adoption and managed-VM creation. Capability-gated storage/network registration, bounded ISO transfer and stopped-VM provisioning use outbound authenticated Core reports. Browser VM consoles use single-use tickets, an outbound host tunnel and a same-origin WebSocket. Central VM power requests (start, shutdown, reboot, force-stop, force-reboot) are durable host operations.

get.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Read-only; safe to retry. Returns CSRF token for same-origin mutations. All authenticated administrator operations have controller-wide scope. Does not extend the idle deadline. A 401 requires sign-in again; session JSON fields are unchanged and contain no expiry timestamps.

post.description: Validates existing administrator credentials and browser origin. Sets __Host-nex_session with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ and no Domain. Each login creates a new session; at most 64 active sessions per service. Sessions expire after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation and eight hours absolutely; GET/HEAD polling does not renew them. Legacy unprefixed cookies are not accepted; sign in again after upgrade. Existing password hashes remain valid; new administrator bootstrap passwords must be nonempty valid UTF-8, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes, without CR, LF or NUL; there is no minimum length or complexity rule. Login admission permits at most five valid-length attempts per one-minute actual peer-IP window, two concurrent password checks per service, and 4096 tracked peers. Forwarded client-IP headers are ignored. Login returns 429 when rate/concurrency/table or 64-session capacity is exhausted; bounded retries must not create an unbounded loop.

post.summary: Probe a host's local API TLS certificate
post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Performs an insecure TLS 1.3 handshake to the given address (default port 9443) purely to capture the leaf certificate nex-core-local presents; it establishes no trust and stores nothing. The operator compares the returned fingerprint, subject and expiry against the physical host before confirming add-host. This never contacts the Controller-to-Core enrollment contract; it only inspects the host's existing local API listener.

post.summary: Add a host by address and root password
post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Replaces manual token enrollment for a reachable host: the operator first confirms the certificate fingerprint returned by probeHost, then submits it here alongside the host's root password. The Controller re-verifies that same fingerprint with a constant-time comparison during its own outbound TLS handshake to the host — a mismatch fails the handshake and returns 502 before the password is ever sent. On a verified connection the Controller signs in to the host's local API (POST /api/local/v1/session), mints a fresh site-bound enrollment token (the same token contract createEnrollmentToken uses), and pushes it to the host's local enrollment endpoint together with the Controller's own served HTTPS certificate (the -tls-cert file, not the host-identity CA) as the trust the host pins for its Controller connection; the host then enrolls with this Controller through the existing agent-enrollment contract and becomes the master of a new pool in this site. The root password is used once for that single sign-in and is never stored, logged, or echoed back, including in error messages. Unknown site_id returns 400. Optional host_id re-enrolls a revoked host whose pool belongs to this site (409 otherwise, checked before any network attempt). A wrong password returns 401; a login rate limit returns 429 with the host's own message. If the host reports it is already enrolled under a different identity, this returns 409 with that host_id — retrying the same add-host call after a lost response is safe and resolves the same way: fetch inventory to see the enrolled host. Any other host-side failure returns 502 naming the controller_url the host was asked to reach, and any token minted for the attempt is deleted. If the Controller process has no served certificate configured, 503 is returned before any host contact; use manual enrollment.

post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Outbound HTTPS; agent must verify Controller identity before transmitting its site-bound token. Provide a signed PEM ECDSA P-256 CSR and nonblank hostname (maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes, no CR/LF/NUL). Identity is host-owned: the host presents the host_id it generated and, as its pool's master, the pool_id and pool_name it keeps, and the Controller adopts them unchanged, so a replacement Controller recovers the pool with its original ID and name. host_id and pool_id must be canonical lowercase UUIDs (or the 64-hex form issued to hosts enrolled before host-owned identity) and pool_name a valid name, else 400. A fresh enrollment creates the pool in the token site with this host as its master, then records the host in that pool in the same transaction (audit pool.create and host.enroll); older agents that present no identity get Controller-minted IDs and a pool named after the hostname, which the response reports for the host to keep. A presented host_id already on record, or a pool_id already held by another master host, is 409: only a token bound to a revoked host may re-issue that host, and it must present that host and its pool (409 otherwise). A separate authenticated Core-local peer flow can subsequently join a member; this enrollment endpoint neither joins members nor changes master. The same key is the same host: a request whose CSR matches a recorded active credential (a retry after a lost response, even with a new token) returns that credential unchanged. Issues a 90-day host-specific client certificate and CA. The token binds to its first CSR; an identical token/CSR retry before token expiry returns the same identity without duplicate enrollment. A different CSR returns 409. After expiry or revocation obtain a new site-bound token; replacement requires explicit revoked host selection. Enrollment has no VM side effects. Compatibility: an older Controller rejects the new fields with 400 (unknown field); upgrade Controller and Core together.

post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0. Outbound mutual TLS authenticates exactly one enrolled, unrevoked host. Versions 1 and 2 are accepted; version 2 starts repository negotiation without storage-repositories-v1, waits for the Controller storage_repositories acknowledgement, persists it, then advertises that capability. Clustered storage has its own v2 acknowledgement: a Core sends neither clustered results nor storage-clustered-iscsi-v2 until it receives storage_clusters_support with that exact capability. The Controller sends that acknowledgement on every v2 preflight. A newly reconnected Core may offer the session-monitor preflight while withholding storage-clustered-iscsi-v2; before its acknowledged follow-up report, Controller clustered routes return retryable 503 negotiation pending without dispatching work or falling back. Core resets this readiness on start, Controller replacement/enrollment and report disconnect, so an older strict Controller sees only the clean preflight; queued Core results remain durable until a matching Controller acknowledges. Persist a strictly increasing sequence across restarts; discard superseded reports. Null/omitted inventory is heartbeat only and never makes old checks healthy. Results refer only to this host operations; acknowledge persisted results before deleting local journal entries. Commands can redeliver and must be reconciled by operation_id. Controller reconnect requires fresh inventory; no automatic VM restart is permitted. Sequence range is 1 through 9223372036854775807. Superseded sequences receive 200 but do not update last-seen or inventory; operation results and command redelivery still reconcile. At most 100 results per report; result error is at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Results for queued, undelivered operations return 409, foreign/unknown operation IDs return 400. Terminal results are acknowledged without rewriting the original outcome. At most 100 pending commands return, in creation order. Inventory fields merge only when inventory observed_at increases; individual checks merge only when their observed_at increases. Controller derives per-check freshness independently from heartbeat freshness. Health changes are recorded as debounced audit transitions (default debounce five seconds, configurable). Reports advertise at most 32 capabilities of up to 100 UTF-8 bytes each. managed-vm-v1 gates new commands; omission prevents managed delivery and a newer sequence clears stored capabilities. Result states include needs_attention for uncertain host effects.

post.description: Administrator-only appliance bootstrap. Persist a stable request_id and random 64-character lowercase hexadecimal enrollment_token before submission. The same request, names and token return the original site without duplicates. Payload changes conflict. An authenticated replay refreshes token expiry to ten minutes without clearing a consumed token's CSR binding; consumed tokens support replay only of the already-enrolled agent CSR through the existing enrollment endpoint. No pool is created here: the appliance host becomes the master of an automatic pool when it enrolls. This does not create or start a VM. Core enrollment remains outbound verified HTTPS protocol v1. Revoked enrollment tokens are not recreated; use explicit recovery.

post.description: Administrator session required. Mutations require same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token; JSON rejects unknown fields and bodies over 1 MiB. Persist request_id before sending. Identical payload replays return the same resource/operation; changed payload conflicts. New work requires a fresh active host in the selected pool advertising managed-vm-v1. Poll resource lists and operations for terminal results. HTTP acceptance is not host completion. Shared bounds, enforced identically on Controller and Core: 1–8 disks of 1–2048 GiB on virtio, sata or scsi with names unique in the VM; at most 8 NICs on virtio or e1000e with unicast lower-case manual MACs; at least 1 vCPU with sockets × cores × threads equal to the count when a topology is given; at least 512 MiB in memory mode dedicated or maximum; uefi or bios; boot orders unique and positive across disks and install media (gaps are allowed, since ejecting media leaves one), with at least one boot device. Controller additionally caps CPU at 64 and memory at 262144 MiB, assigns the UUID and refuses capacity above the host's observed CPU or memory. The host decides everything its own record answers: VM name and MAC uniqueness against its managed journal and libvirt domains, and dedicated-memory admission against total host memory, are reported as a failed vm-create result with the reason (visible in Task history), not as an HTTP refusal. Storage, network and ISO must have succeeded on this host and pool. The install ISO may be on any verified storage on that host; it need not share a repository with the VM disks. Core journals effects and reconciles per-disk ownership before replay; needs_attention preserves uncertain resources for manual recovery. start_after_create is honoured by the host inside the same creation: once the definition is verified the creation has succeeded, and Core starts the guest once, recording the outcome in the journal entry's start field so a retry never starts it twice. A failed automatic start keeps the VM as a normal stopped managed VM and is reported as a separate failed vm-power outcome (<operation-id>:start, 'VM created but not started: <reason>') in Task history; start it from the Power controls. autostart is a libvirt property set while the stopped VM is defined. No console, overwrite, automatic cleanup of ambiguous disks or guest installation. Core requires 2 GiB available host RAM reserve and verifies KVM/x86-64 and machine-type libvirt capabilities; uefi requires advertised EFI firmware. Failed/uncertain VM names remain reserved; there is no retry/deletion endpoint. A non-empty drivers_media_id requires the host to report vm-media-drivers-drive-v1 (409 "the selected host agent does not support a driver disc drive; upgrade Nex Core") and a succeeded ISO import on the same host and pool (404 "the driver disc ISO is not registered and verified on the selected host and pool"); both are checked after the replay check.

post.summary: Discover a storage source from Nex Core
post.description: Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. The Controller validates pool/host scope then relays one bounded discovery request only to the addressed authenticated Core advertising storage-repositories-v1 and storage-discovery-v1. Discovery is an observation, never a registration: it cannot create directories, mount or log in a source, retain iSCSI nodes/sessions, change repository state or journal work. The Controller keeps the request (including SMB/CHAP credentials when supplied) only in an in-memory request/response relay, deletes it on Core delivery, result, browser cancellation or the 30-second deadline, and writes neither credentials nor candidates to SQLite, a journal, audit log or cache. Core limits work to eight seconds and returns sanitized candidates only; no credentials, device paths, mount options or command output. A 200 result may be empty, failed or stale; 504 is stale when no Core result arrives before the deadline. Retry with a new request ID after timeout or cancellation.

A Core that never offers clustered support remains 409. The Controller forwards one transient status request only after acknowledgement and retains no cluster configuration, job or secret. A 200 is the Core's current durable operation projection; a 504 means the Core did not answer within 30 seconds and is ambiguous, so retry this GET rather than assuming setup stopped. The Controller HTTPS write deadline is 45 seconds only to leave delivery margin for this existing 30-second relay contract; it does not extend Core work.

post.summary: Ask Core to verify one cluster fence
post.description: Administrator session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. request_id identifies the destructive attempt; host_id is the target, and fence_confirmation must be exactly FENCE <host_id>. The Controller validates target capability and relays the confirmation transiently to the pool master. It creates no durable fence intent. An immediate accepted response is not a proof: Core records its durable cluster operation as verifying_fence with a request-bound unverified pending proof, and performs the actual exclusion observation only at the executor. Browser input cannot claim a proof. An early failed observation is uncertain. The unchanged relay deadline is 30 seconds; the Controller's 45-second HTTPS write deadline only leaves response-delivery margin. A timeout is ambiguous: the UI closes the dialog and disables that target until a successful Core status refresh, without automatic retry. A refreshed failed or uncertain proof may be manually reverified only with a new request_id and a new exact confirmation; Core retains the prior proof. A pending unverified proof remains disabled. This is existing recovery behavior, not a new interface.

put.summary: Replace a VM's definition on its assigned host
put.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token. Persist request_id before sending; the same id replays the same durable operation, a different body under the same id is 409. The body is the complete desired definition (the same shape as creation); Controller validates its shape and references like creation, refuses immutable changes (an existing disk's storage, size or provisioning), and, when the VM is observed running, changes that need it stopped (name, CPU, memory, firmware, machine type, any boot order, an existing disk's bus, an existing interface's network, model, MAC or MTU, or adding a SATA disk); interfaces are matched by effective MAC: when the request names any current interface by its effective MAC (as the VM list reports it, and as the bundled editor sends every existing interface), every interface with an empty MAC is new; when it names none, an empty MAC is matched by position and the request is refused with 400 if it removes, reorders or changes an interface at an existing index, while an unchanged interface keeps the current address at its position. Clients that send any existing interface's MAC must send all of them, or an omitted one is replaced by a new interface. Controller freezes every automatic MAC into the definition before its stop-first check, drawing new ones from the VM's derived range at the first index above the highest one the current definition uses that no requested or current interface holds, or the lowest free index when none above is free, so a new interface never takes the address of one removed in the same edit, nor, unless the highest-index interface was removed or index 255 is in use, of one removed in an earlier edit; then it queues a vm-update command at revision current + 1 for the host's next report. Name and MAC uniqueness against other VMs and dedicated-memory admission are checked by the host against its journal and libvirt, as for creation. Core applies live what a running guest can take (adding or removing VirtIO/SCSI disks and interfaces, inserting, swapping or ejecting the ISO, description, guest OS hint and autostart) and redefines a shut-off guest from the regenerated XML; removed disks are detached and their files retained, never deleted. While validating a running guest's edit, before allocating any disk or changing any device, Core compares the live and persistent domains and reports the vm-update operation failed, changing nothing, with "network interface MAC <mac> is still attached to the running VM; wait for the guest to release it or stop the VM, then save again" when an added interface's MAC is still on a live interface that the guest has not released, changing nothing. The host reports the new definition as current and Controller refreshes its mirror from that report; poll operations for the result. One vm-update, vm-power or vm-media request per VM may be in flight.

get.description: Administrator session; read-only and safe to retry. Relays the query to the host over a stats channel the host dials out (first query waits up to one report heartbeat, then the channel is reused and closes after 5 minutes idle). The history is recorded and kept by Nex Core; the Controller stores nothing. Requires the host to be fresh, not revoked and to report usage-history-v1.

parameters.description: live returns up to the last 120 one-second samples and starts, or renews for 2 minutes, one-second sampling of this object on the host; poll it about once a second. The other ranges read stored history.
