post.summary: Attach the host's outbound stats channel
post.description: Core sends this over its enrolled mTLS connection with Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: nex-stats after receiving stats_channels in a report response. The token must name a pending channel for this exact host. After 101 the Controller writes HTTP/1.1 GET /stats?object=vm&id=<uuid>&range=<range> or GET /stats?object=host&range=<range> requests on the connection and Core answers each in order with a StatsHistory (200) or {"error"} (400 invalid query, 404 no history). Either side closes the connection on idle, restart or protocol error. Core never listens for inbound stats connections.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Stats channel token from the report response.

101.description: Channel attached; Controller-originated HTTP/1.1 queries follow.

200.description: Not returned; the channel is the 101 response.

400.description: Missing Upgrade: nex-stats.

401.description: Missing, expired, invalid, or revoked credentials.

404.description: Channel token unknown, expired, for another host, or already attached.

500.description: Connection cannot be upgraded.

AdminSession.name: __Host-nex_session
AdminSession.description: Administrator session cookie __Host-nex_session, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict, Path=/ with no Domain. Expires after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation or eight hours absolutely. GET/HEAD polling does not extend idle lifetime; mutations also require matching Origin and X-CSRF-Token. At most 64 active sessions per service. Legacy unprefixed cookies are refused; sign in again after upgrading.

x-session-policy.idle_refresh: authenticated mutations after Origin/CSRF validation; GET and HEAD never extend it

HostCertificate.description: Unique signed host certificate; current enrollment and revocation are checked on each request.

master_host_id.description: Host that controls this pool. Empty only for databases migrated from the removed manual pool creation with no host.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

error.description: Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes; absence means no error detail supplied.

freshness.description: Controller-derived elapsed receipt freshness; agent input is ignored. Never infer a current healthy check solely from fresh host connection.

Check.description: Per-probe health distinct from management connection freshness. observed_at marks the check result; last_success is absent until success is observed; error carries actionable failure details.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

kind.description: Interface classification for uplink selection; absent from older agents.

master.description: Bridge or bond this device is enslaved to; absent when standalone or from older agents.

parent.description: For 802.1Q VLAN devices, the raw device they sit on.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

available_bytes.description: Available filesystem bytes when known; absent for raw block devices or unsupported capacity observations.

id.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

state.description: Observed libvirt state; maximum 100 UTF-8 bytes.

guest.description: Host observation of the running guest through its virtio channels; absent for VMs that are not running and from Core builds that predate guest observation.

usage.description: Host observation of a running VM's resource consumption; absent for VMs that are not running, from Core builds that predate usage observation, and whenever the host could not sample the VM within its probe deadline.

observed_at.description: When the sample was taken, not when it was reported. A host that could not resample a VM re-reports the previous sample unchanged, so this is the only honest statement of how old the numbers are.

sample_window_ms.description: Wall-clock gap the CPU rate averages over, floored at 1; zero when cpu_percent is absent. Rejected above 300000.

cpu_percent.description: Whole percent of the VM's own allocated vCPUs, averaged over sample_window_ms; 100 means every vCPU was busy throughout. Absent until a second sample exists, so a VM that just started or whose counter reset reports no rate rather than a wrong one. Clamped at 1000.

memory_assigned_bytes.description: What the guest currently may use. Allocation, never usage.

memory_host_bytes.description: Resident host memory the VM's process occupies: what the VM costs the host, not what the guest uses. Absent when libvirt could not read it without waiting for another operation on this VM.

disk_used_bytes.description: Space the VM's own disk images occupy in their repository now. CD drives, firmware variable stores and images outside the per-VM directory are not counted. Absent when libvirt could not read it without waiting for another operation on this VM.

disk_capacity_bytes.description: Virtual size the guest sees; a thin disk grows towards it. Absent under the same condition as disk_used_bytes.

cpu_models.description: Named QEMU CPU models libvirt marks usable=yes on this Core host's default q35 machine. Availability list only, not durable configuration; unusable baselines are omitted.

os_version.description: PRETTY_NAME from /etc/os-release. On Nex Core this is "Nex Core <version>", the single product version (the nex-core-local package). Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

agent_version.description: nex-core-local package version; equals the Nex Core version on Nex Core hosts. Maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

managed.description: Pool-scoped configuration this host has durably applied, read from the Core managed journal; null or omitted when the host holds nothing. On each managed report Controller adopts, under actor system, every entry it does not hold (request_id adopt-<kind>:<host>:<id>, kind storage-register | network-register | iso-import | vm-create), reusing the resource ID and recording the operation as already succeeded without dispatching a command; it also rebuilds its appliances record from appliances and records outcomes as operations. Entries that duplicate an existing ID, storage path, network (kind, source) or VM name, invalid entries, entries whose references are not adopted on the host and VMs listed in missing_vms are not adopted; each leaves one needs_attention operation and an audit entry (see ManagedState). The host's managed-journal check reports failed when a journal file could not be read (that file is skipped, the rest is still reported) and managed-vms reports failed when a journaled VM is missing from libvirt.

checks.description: At most 256 checks with unique names within a report.

Inventory.description: Read-only host observations; byte quantities are bytes, CPU count is logical CPUs, timestamps are RFC3339 UTC. NIC state describes a local link, not end-to-end reachability. VM state is observed libvirt state, not guest application health. Null lists mean no observations supplied. Controller retains newer inventory resource timestamps and independently newer per-check timestamps; a newer report sequence does not freshen an unchanged or older sample.

connection.description: unknown before any report, fresh within configured stale threshold, stale otherwise, revoked after administrator revocation. Restart cannot establish freshness from persisted wall-clock time alone. Controller default stale threshold is 30 seconds and is configurable; this is not a failure or failover deadline.

last_seen.description: Controller wall-clock receipt time of newest accepted report; null until a report arrives. Freshness is tracked using elapsed time in the active process.

capabilities.description: Last accepted sequenced report capabilities; managed-vm-v1 is required for new managed-VM work. Host connectivity freshness is checked separately.

csr_pem.description: Signed PEM CERTIFICATE REQUEST using an ECDSA P-256 key; no trailing PEM data.

hostname.description: Nonblank, maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes, no CR/LF/NUL.

host_id.description: Host-owned identity: the UUID this host generated on its first enrollment (canonical lowercase form) and keeps across Controllers. Hosts enrolled before host-owned identity present their Controller-issued 64-hex ID instead. Omitted only by older agents; the Controller then mints one.

pool_id.description: UUID of the pool this host is master of, generated by the host with host_id and kept across Controllers. Omitted by older agents or hosts that adopted a Controller-minted pool before presenting one; the Controller then mints or keeps the pool.

pool_name.description: Name of the pool held by the pool master, its hostname at first enrollment. Nonblank, maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes, no CR/LF/NUL. Defaults to hostname when omitted.

host_id.description: Equals the presented host_id when one was presented.

pool_id.description: Pool the host is master of; equals the presented pool_id when one was presented. Absent from rotation responses.

pool_name.description: Name of that pool. Absent from rotation responses.

csr_pem.description: Signed PEM CERTIFICATE REQUEST using an ECDSA P-256 key; no trailing PEM data.

vm.description: The full VM definition for vm-create (revision 0) and vm-update (revision current + 1).

error.description: At most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; omit for successful checks.

observed_at.description: Agent-reported result time; controller operation updated_at records receipt/commit time. Not proof of guest application health.

version.description: Version 1 is the legacy managed-VM report. A Core starts storage negotiation with version 2 but without storage-repositories-v1, waits for storage_repositories acknowledgement, persists it, then advertises the capability.

inventory.description: Omit or null for heartbeat only; prior inventory remains unchanged and is not made healthy.

capabilities.description: Advertised on every report. managed-vm-v1 enables managed command delivery. storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 offers the additive clustered session-monitor projection; it must be acknowledged through storage_clusters_support before Core sends that projection. Omission or null disables managed delivery for this report; a newer sequence also replaces stored capabilities.

storage_discoveries.description: One-shot sanitized results from prior report-response discovery requests. Never journaled or adopted.

storage_clusters.description: Transient results for addressed clustered-storage requests, emitted only after the exact v2 storage_clusters_support acknowledgement. session_monitor_ready and monitor-stage members are included only after the offered storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 extension is acknowledged. The result exposes Core-owned durable operation state but is not Controller state.

ReportRequest.description: Version and sequence are required by runtime validation. Results may be omitted or null and defaults to no results. Inventory may be omitted or null for heartbeat only. Clustered results and storage-clustered-iscsi-v2 are withheld until this Controller connection acknowledges storage_clusters_support. The additive session-monitor members are withheld unless the Core offered and the Controller acknowledged storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1. Both acknowledgements reset after a cluster preflight failure, reconnect or Controller re-enrolment. Version-one reports retain existing non-storage behavior.

consoles.description: Console pairings to attach now; omitted when none. Not durable operations: they are delivered once and never journaled.

credential_offers.description: Opaque, addressed offers only; no credential bytes.

storage_repositories.description: Controller-first acknowledgement of protocol v2 storage support.

storage_clusters_support.description: Controller acknowledgement for the clustered v2 envelope. The base capability enables clustered results; storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 is returned only when the Core offered it and enables the additive session-monitor report projection.

storage_discoveries.description: One-shot addressed Core observations. Controller removes each request from its bounded relay on delivery.

storage_clusters.description: One-shot addressed relay requests for a Core that has acknowledged and advertises storage-clustered-iscsi-v2. Controller deletes them after delivery, completion, cancellation, or deadline.

stats_channels.description: Sent only to a host that offered usage-history-v1 when a browser query needs a stats channel and none is open. Delivered once, never journaled.

resource_id.description: The resource the action applied to, such as a site, pool, host or VM ID. VM requests record the VM ID; older vm-power, vm-media, vm-update and vm-delete rows keep an operation or internal row ID.

detail.description: Actionable detail for debounced health transitions when present.

password.description: Existing administrator password, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Existing password hashes remain valid.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL.

host_id.description: Optional revoked host to re-enroll; its pool must belong to site_id.

address.description: Hostname or IP, optionally with :port (default 9443). No scheme, path, or userinfo.

fingerprint.description: sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters> over the leaf certificate's DER encoding.

subject.description: Leaf certificate subject, for operator confirmation only.

address.description: Hostname or IP, optionally with :port (default 9443). No scheme, path, or userinfo.

fingerprint.description: sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters>, as returned by probeHost and confirmed by the operator.

root_password.description: Used once to sign in to the host's local API; never stored, logged, or echoed. 1-1024 bytes, no NUL.

controller_url.description: This Controller's own HTTPS origin, reachable from the host, given to it as its enrollment target.

host_id.description: Optional revoked host to re-enroll; its pool must belong to this site.

pool_id.description: The automatic pool the enrollment created or, on re-enrollment, kept.

host_id.description: Present when the host reported it is already enrolled.

request_id.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL.

enrollment_token.description: Caller-generated secret persisted before sending; never log or expose in operation results.

pool_id.description: Optional; when supplied it must equal the host's pool.

vm_id.description: Stable lowercase nonzero libvirt UUID; adoption preserves identity.

guest.description: Latest host guest observation for a VM observed running in a fresh report; omitted otherwise.

usage.description: Host observation of a running VM's resource consumption; absent for VMs that are not running, from Core builds that predate usage observation, and whenever the host could not sample the VM within its probe deadline.

ManagedAppliance.description: Unified VM listing. Existing adopted appliances preserve role=controller and protected=true without creation spec/status. Generic guest entries add spec and operation_id/status/error; state/freshness always come from fresh successful libvirt observations independently of creation status.

directory.description: Validated existing relative subdirectory beneath the original NFS export; spaces are supported, traversal, backslashes and control characters are rejected.

mount_path.description: Original existing ZFS dataset mount path. It rejects Unicode whitespace/control characters, percent and backslash because Core uses it as a systemd What value.

share.description: Ordinary share name: letters, numbers, internal spaces and ._$:()-; no leading/trailing whitespace or path/command/unit syntax.

directory.description: Validated existing relative subdirectory below the SMB share, including spaces; never an SMB path. Traversal, backslashes and control characters are rejected.

ISCSIStorageSource.description: exclusive is the legacy single-writer profile and needs exclusive_target. clustered_gfs2 instead requires cluster_id, lock_table and three to five unique eligible hosts, rejects exclusive_target, and only accepts an existing GFS2 filesystem; Core never formats it.

ISCSIStorageSourceIntent.description: Client iSCSI intent. Core chooses mount_path only after allocating the repository ID.

StorageSourceIntent.description: Non-secret client source selection. Exactly one backend is required for a typed repository.

filesystem_id.description: New Core-observed identities use the NFSv4 kernel protocol FSID profile nfs4:<mounted-server-address-hex>:<port-hex>:<fsid-major-hex>:<fsid-minor-hex>. Core binds that profile to stat.Dev and one matching /proc/fs/nfsfs/volumes row, then verifies the requested source. Missing or ambiguous rows fail closed; a zero protocol FSID is valid. Address changes fail closed and are not NFS HA failover. Preserved legacy statfs identities remain representable, are not auto-upgraded, and fail closed.
Diagnostic CIFS filesystem ID; it is not durable across reconnects.

marker_id.description: Core-created atomic durable share-root marker for new registrations. Core verifies it with the exact SMB source/options after reconnect. Absent only on preserved legacy records, which retain strict filesystem-ID failure behavior and are not auto-upgraded.

virsh_uri.description: For virsh, exactly qemu:///system or qemu+ssh://<ssh_login>@<endpoint>[:<ssh_port>]/system. The latter must match the pinned SSH fields; it rejects passwords, query strings, fragments and every other URI path. An omitted URI port is valid only when ssh_port is 22.

StorageClusterFence.description: Closed Core fence profile. credential_ref and ssh_host_key_ref are opaque names for root-only Core secrets, never secret bytes; arbitrary commands and arguments are not accepted. virsh is development-only and remains unaccepted for native production use.

request_id.description: Optional stable ID of the actual destructive fence attempt. A Core verifies this binding before accepting a peer receipt.

StorageClusterFenceStatus.description: Core-recorded result of an actual fence/exclusion observation, bound to a request ID when destructive work was attempted and to an exact configuration generation and digest.

StorageClusterConfig.description: Core-owned clustered-GFS2 projection. Controller relay input never grants a caller-owned device path, mount path, proof, or secret; Core derives/verifies those native details.

session_monitor_ready.description: Authenticated member attestation that the fixed local transport-monitor wrapper and CLI are installed and passed a successful live exact portal/IQN session probe. It is distinct from aggregate GFS2 or cluster health, and is projected to Controller only after storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 is acknowledged.

StorageClusterRequest.description: Authenticated Controller/Core report envelope. It is transient at Controller; Core persists accepted configuration and operation state.

StorageClusterCredentialRef.description: Secret-free reference to a one-time Core credential handoff.

StorageClusterOperation.description: v2 operation projection. members are typed host-bound reports, never an unordered flattened status list. degraded is a Core-observed post-activation runtime state, not an activation receipt or client action.

StorageClusterMemberReport.description: Core-observed member report bound to one configured host and exact clustered-storage configuration. monitor is sent only after the offered storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 extension is acknowledged. The Controller rejects duplicate, non-member or mismatched bindings.

expected_generation.description: Optional optimistic generation. Omit or use zero for a candidate repository whose Core allocation has not yet assigned a generation.

StorageClusterCredentialRequest.description: One-time secret handoff. secret is bounded to 64 KiB and is never returned; username is optional.

StorageCredentials.description: Transient credential bytes only. Optional domain is the SMB workgroup or AD domain used with username/secret. The selected operation validates the applicable secret form; inventory, journals, results and diagnostics never carry these fields.

retire_eligible.description: Core's current redacted eligibility observation. Core rechecks references before a retire command takes effect.

StorageClusterSupport.description: Controller-first acknowledgement for the clustered-storage v2 envelope. Return storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 only when the Core offered it; otherwise return storage-clustered-iscsi-v2.

identity.description: Core-canonical secret-free identity observed after member preparation.

locking.description: Member proved the shared non-blocking lock against the master for this generation.

PoolStorageReservationRequest.description: Authenticated member-to-master peer request. The master binds the reservation to the mTLS member identity, not a client host field.

PoolStorageReservationRelease.description: Peer DELETE query shape. release_unused is used only by a member after its healthy serialized Core journal proves no managed VM disk or ISO reference remains.

StorageRegistration.description: Core-owned repository configuration and observation. A repository has one selected host in this release; shared is a capability observation, never placement permission. Source identity, access, capacity and health are Core observations; a missing or replaced mount blocks writes and never falls back to a mountpoint. For ZFS, source.zfs.mount_path remains the existing dataset mount and path is the Core-owned /var/lib/nex-storage/<repository-id> bind alias used by VM disks; detach removes only that alias, never ZFS properties. Credentials remain Core-local and inventory reports only presence. A fresh Controller adopts these records from Inventory.managed.storage.

source.description: Bridge name used by guest interfaces (derived <uplink>v<vlan> for kind vlan) or libvirt network name.

uplink.description: Uplink NIC name: required for kind vlan; set on kind bridge when the registration was created automatically for the untagged network of a bridge on a physical port.

NetworkRegistration.description: Pool guest network on one host: an existing bridge, an active libvirt network, or a Core-created VLAN bridge (kind vlan) on an uplink NIC. VLAN bridges are additive; the management bridge, addresses and routes are never changed. The host self-registers the untagged default network of every host bridge on a physical NIC or bond (<port> untagged, kind bridge, uplink recorded) in its own journal with host-generated IDs, at agent start and when a new uplink appears; Controller creates registrations itself only by adoption (actor system): any network the host reports in Inventory.managed.networks that Controller does not hold (request_id adopt-network:<host>:<id>, ID and name preserved). A bridge or libvirt network already held by another registration on that host is a failed host result, not an HTTP 409.

size_bytes.description: Zero until a URL download completes; applied media is at least 32774 bytes.

url.description: Command-only public HTTP(S) source URL. Omitted from client responses and applied host inventory. Requires iso-download-v1.

count.description: vCPUs presented to the guest. Both sides require at least 1; Controller caps the request at 64 and refuses more than the host reports.

sockets.description: Sockets, or 0 with cores and threads for the default topology.

cores.description: Cores per socket, or 0 for the default topology.

threads.description: Threads per core, or 0 for the default topology.

model.description: host-passthrough (the default) gives the guest the host CPU; host-model describes it for later migration. Any other value must appear in the assigned host's current Inventory.cpu_models (usable named models only) and Core refuses it otherwise; named values use libvirt custom/exact mode with partial feature checking and fallback forbidden.

VMCPU.description: vCPU count, optional topology and CPU model. Sockets, cores and threads all 0 select the default topology of one socket, count cores and one thread; otherwise each must be at least 1 and sockets × cores × threads must equal count. JSON Schema cannot express that product, so Controller and Core both enforce it in protocol.ValidateVMSpec.

mode.description: dedicated preallocates and locks the ceiling in host RAM while running: memory and currentMemory at size_mib, no balloon, and memoryBacking with immediate allocation, locked and nosharepages. Stopped VMs release physical RAM but retain their Nex capacity commitment. QEMU overhead is locked too. Requires updated Core; existing VMs need full shutdown, a successful stopped vm-update save and start. Legacy dedicated live edits fail before device effects with a stop-and-save instruction. Upgrade, autostart or guest reboot alone does not rewrite old definitions. maximum caps without reserving: the same ceiling plus a virtio balloon with free page reporting, so the guest returns pages it frees. Reclaim requires the balloon driver running in the guest (built into Linux; virtio-win guest tools on Windows); without it the guest drifts to the ceiling and holds it. There is no pressure-driven reclaim daemon.

size_mib.description: Memory ceiling in MiB. Both sides require at least 512; Controller caps the request at 262144.

VMMemory.description: Memory ceiling and how the host treats it. size_mib is the ceiling in both modes and host capacity preflight uses that ceiling in both modes: a VM that cannot reach its ceiling is refused. dedicated additionally counts against committed capacity; maximum reserves nothing and is allowed to oversubscribe.

storage_id.description: Registered storage that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool. Core resolves it by resource ID, not by pool/host ID, so it survives Controller replacement.

name.description: Operator-facing disk name, unique within the VM. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, starting with a letter or digit; it is not a path.

bus.description: virtio needs guest drivers (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows); sata and scsi work without them.

thin.description: true creates a sparse qcow2 that grows on use; false preallocates the full size.

boot_order.description: 0 keeps the disk out of the boot order. Non-zero values are unique across every disk and boot.media_boot_order and number the boot devices from 1 with no gaps.

VMDisk.description: One virtual disk, created inside the VM's own exclusive directory on its storage target. Disks are never shared or reused: Core checks exclusive ownership for every disk and free space per storage target, summing the disks that land on the same target.

network_id.description: Registered network that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool, resolved by resource ID.

model.description: Which network card the guest sees. virtio is paravirtualised: fastest and lowest host CPU, but the guest needs a driver (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows). e1000 and e1000e emulate Intel gigabit cards nearly every OS already drives, for guests and installers that cannot see a virtio adapter, at higher host CPU. rtl8139 emulates a 100 Mbit card for guests too old for a gigabit driver; the limit is the emulated hardware. vmxnet3 is VMware's paravirtualised adapter, for guests already carrying VMware drivers.

mac.description: Empty derives a stable MAC from the VM ID and the interface index (protocol.DerivedMAC: the 52:54:00 locally administered prefix, two octets of sha256(id) and the index), which never collides across a VM's at most 8 interfaces. A manual address must be six octets in canonical lower-case colon form and unicast; the pattern encodes the cleared multicast bit as an even second hex digit. All-zero addresses are refused, addresses are unique within the VM, and Controller additionally enforces uniqueness across the pool by plain string comparison. The VM list reports the effective address, and an edit freezes every automatic address into the definition (drawn from the VM's derived range above the highest index the VM uses, or the lowest free index when none above is free), so interfaces keep their identity across later edits.

mtu.description: Interface MTU, or 0 for the network's own. Accepted only when model is virtio: QEMU communicates an MTU to the guest through virtio's host_mtu feature and libvirt sizes the host tap to match, while the emulated models have no equivalent and would leave the guest on its own default. A value on any other model is refused rather than silently applied to the host side only. The floor is the IPv6 minimum MTU and the ceiling the largest jumbo frame common NICs accept; every device along the path must agree or traffic is dropped without an error.

VMNIC.description: One virtual network interface on a registered pool network. A VM may have none and at most 8.

firmware.description: uefi is the default and requires EFI firmware advertised by the host's libvirt domain capabilities; bios stays selectable.

machine.description: Empty selects Core's default machine type (q35).

media_boot_order.description: 0 keeps the CD drive out of the boot order; any other value joins the disks' contiguous 1..N numbering. Every VM has the drive, so the order is kept while it is empty and an ISO can be ejected from a running guest.

secure_boot.description: UEFI Secure Boot. Omitted means on with the Microsoft keys enrolled, which is exactly what libvirt already selected for every UEFI VM defined before this field existed, so a definition re-sent unchanged keeps the firmware its guest was installed with. off selects the plain OVMF build with no enrolled keys, for unsigned boot media or drivers. Requires uefi; on with bios is rejected. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not offer a matching firmware build, naming the setting rather than passing libvirt's firmware-selection error through. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off.

tpm.description: Emulated TPM. 2.0 adds a tpm-crb device backed by swtpm; omitted and none add no device, so a definition written before this field keeps exactly the devices it had. Windows 11 requires a TPM and refuses to install without one. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not advertise the emulator backend, rather than defining a device that cannot start. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off, and REMOVING a TPM is refused outright at any time: anything the guest sealed to it, including a Windows BitLocker key, would be lost, and libvirt cleans TPM state by iterating the devices the persistent definition still carries, so a redefine without it would orphan that state.

VMBoot.description: Firmware, Secure Boot, TPM, machine type and the install media's place in the boot order. Boot order is per device (libvirt forbids mixing per-device boot with an os/boot device list), so at least one disk or the install media must carry a non-zero order.

id.description: Controller-assigned stable UUID; identity is preserved across Controller replacement and later migration.

name.description: Nonblank VM name, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (the byte limit is additionally enforced by Controller and Core). Spaces, case, dots, punctuation and Unicode are preserved exactly. Slashes, control characters and XML-invalid U+FFFE/U+FFFF are rejected. Core checks uniqueness on the host, journals the name and reports it for Controller adoption; failed or uncertain creations retain their reservation. Upgrade Controller and Core together to use the expanded naming syntax.

description.description: Free-text operator note, at most 4096 characters.

guest_os.description: Guest OS hint recorded for display and guest-tools advice; empty leaves it unset. It installs nothing and does not change the VM devices: disk bus and NIC model are chosen per device.

disks.description: One to eight disks; names unique within the VM.

media_id.description: Install ISO (Media.id), empty for none. The ISO must be imported and verified on the placement host; it may live on any storage that host can read and does not need to share a repository with the VM's disks. Every VM has the CD drive, so a non-zero boot.media_boot_order does not require media_id: an emptied drive keeps its place in the boot order.

drivers_media_id.description: ISO in the VM's second CD drive, for a driver disc an installer needs alongside its install media - a Windows guest installing to a VirtIO disk needs the virtio-win ISO here. Empty leaves that drive empty; the drive itself always exists on a host reporting vm-media-drivers-drive-v1. Must differ from media_id.

start_after_create.description: Honoured by the host inside the creation, after the definition is verified, so the creation itself has succeeded whether or not the flag is set: Core starts the guest exactly once and records the outcome in the journal entry's start field. A failed automatic start leaves the VM defined and stopped as a normal managed VM (power, console and media work; a replacement Controller adopts it) and is reported by the host as its own outcome with ID <operation-id>:start, kind vm-power, status failed and error 'VM created but not started: <reason>', which Controller records in Task history. A creation interrupted at the start step reconciles by observing libvirt: running means started, otherwise that outcome reads 'interrupted before the automatic start completed'. A failed or uncertain creation never boots. Controller issues no follow-on power request. Must be false in an edit.

autostart.description: libvirt autostart, set while the stopped guest is defined so the host starts this VM on boot. It is not a start.

revision.description: Definition revision: 0 at creation, current + 1 for each edit. Core refuses any other value, so a stale edit after Controller replacement fails instead of applying an old definition. Reported back in Inventory.managed.vms with the current definition.

VMCreateSpec.description: The complete VM specification: Controller-assigned UUID and pool membership with separate host assignment, identity, CPU, memory, every disk and network interface, boot and install media, and the two lifecycle switches. Creation defines a stopped VM and never boots it. Dependencies must have succeeded on this host and pool. Both sides validate the shared bounds through protocol.ValidateVMSpec; Controller owns identity, reference existence, pool-wide MAC uniqueness and capacity.

StorageRegistrationRequest.description: A path-only body remains the protocol-v1 local-directory registration. Typed v2 repositories select kind and exactly one source. Core allocates the repository ID, canonicalizes identity and rechecks access before use.

StorageRegistrationIntent.description: Desired source configuration for a repository update. Core-owned ID, pool, host, operation status, identity, generation and observations are omitted; Core preserves its repository identity and validates the supplied intent.

source.description: kind bridge/network only: existing bridge or active libvirt network name. Omit for kind vlan; Controller derives the bridge name <uplink>v<vlan>.

uplink.description: kind vlan only: host NIC or bond name that carries the VLAN, at most 10 characters; it must appear in the host inventory as physical or bond (or without a kind from an older agent).

vlan.description: kind vlan only: 802.1Q tag; 0 uses the uplink untagged, which Core refuses when the host has addresses on it.

NetworkRegistrationRequest.description: Exactly one shape: kind bridge/network with source, or kind vlan with uplink and vlan. Mixed fields are rejected with 400.

id.description: Omit; Controller generates the VM UUID.

name.description: Nonblank VM name, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (the byte limit is additionally enforced by Controller and Core). Spaces, case, dots, punctuation and Unicode are preserved exactly. Slashes, control characters and XML-invalid U+FFFE/U+FFFF are rejected. Core checks uniqueness on the host, journals the name and reports it for Controller adoption; failed or uncertain creations retain their reservation. Upgrade Controller and Core together to use the expanded naming syntax.

description.description: Free-text operator note, at most 4096 characters.

guest_os.description: Guest OS hint recorded for display and guest-tools advice; empty leaves it unset. It installs nothing and does not change the VM devices: disk bus and NIC model are chosen per device.

disks.description: One to eight disks; names unique within the VM.

media_id.description: Install ISO (Media.id), empty for none. The ISO must be imported and verified on the placement host; it may live on any storage that host can read and does not need to share a repository with the VM's disks. Every VM has the CD drive, so a non-zero boot.media_boot_order does not require media_id: an emptied drive keeps its place in the boot order.

drivers_media_id.description: ISO in the VM's second CD drive, for a driver disc an installer needs alongside its install media - a Windows guest installing to a VirtIO disk needs the virtio-win ISO here. Empty leaves that drive empty; the drive itself always exists on a host reporting vm-media-drivers-drive-v1. Must differ from media_id.

start_after_create.description: Honoured by the host inside the creation, after the definition is verified, so the creation itself has succeeded whether or not the flag is set: Core starts the guest exactly once and records the outcome in the journal entry's start field. A failed automatic start leaves the VM defined and stopped as a normal managed VM (power, console and media work; a replacement Controller adopts it) and is reported by the host as its own outcome with ID <operation-id>:start, kind vm-power, status failed and error 'VM created but not started: <reason>', which Controller records in Task history. A creation interrupted at the start step reconciles by observing libvirt: running means started, otherwise that outcome reads 'interrupted before the automatic start completed'. A failed or uncertain creation never boots. Controller issues no follow-on power request.

autostart.description: libvirt autostart, set while the stopped guest is defined so the host starts this VM on boot. It is not a start.

storage.description: Succeeded storage registrations from the host journal.

networks.description: Succeeded network registrations from the host journal.

media.description: Succeeded ISO imports from the host journal.

vms.description: Current VM definitions from the host journal: for each VM this host holds, the highest succeeded revision (creation is revision 0, each vm-update one more, and vm-media changes update the current entry), which is what a replaced Controller re-adopts by resource ID and what an existing Controller refreshes its mirror from on every report.

missing_vms.description: IDs of entries in vms whose persistent domain libvirt no longer lists (for example after an out-of-band undefine). The journal still holds them; Controller records each as a needs_attention operation instead of adopting it, and the host's managed-vms check reports failed. Omitted when libvirt lists every VM or cannot answer.

deleted_vms.description: Intentional VM deletions from succeeded vm-delete journal entries. Controller deletes its vm-create mirror for each tombstone. Distinct from missing_vms (accidental undefine while the journal still expects the VM).

appliances.description: Controller appliance VMs this host deployed through its local appliance engine, from that engine's deploy journal. Controller rebuilds its appliances record from them (insert when missing, keyed by VM UUID; moved to the reporting host when the previous owner is revoked) once healthy libvirt observes the VM, so a replaced Controller lists the appliance as the protected Controller VM again.

outcomes.description: Queued commands and terminal managed-journal outcomes, plus failed automatic-start results under <operation-id>:start. Orphaned non-storage work remains needs_attention. Core's serialized periodic lane retries at most one due pending/needs_attention storage-* original journal entry per minute, retains its original result and excludes definitive failures. Exact Core outcomes update matching nonterminal Controller operations; a replacement Controller adopts unknown operations as passive rows (actor system, request_id adopt-outcome:<host>:<operation_id>) and never redispatches them. The maximum covers 10000 execution journal entries, 10000 derived start results and 10000 additional retained agent commands; duplicate operation IDs are removed by Core.

credential_receipts.description: Redacted Core-owned receipt metadata for adoption; it never contains credential bytes.

ManagedState.description: Every succeeded registration and VM definition from the Core managed journal, plus the host's appliance deployments, queued work and terminal outcomes; at most 10000 entries per resource list and 30000 outcomes; each list is omitted when empty. Pool, host and resource IDs inside entries are host-owned and stable across Controllers: a host's self-registered default entry carries its pool ID when the host knows it (hosts enrolled with host-owned identity), otherwise its host ID as a placeholder until adoption. Adoption records each entry under the host's current pool and host, which is a no-op for hosts that presented their own identity at enrollment; that is how a replaced Controller recovers a pool from its master. Entries the Controller already holds under the same ID and kind are silently current. Any other entry it cannot adopt (invalid, conflicting ID/path/source/name, references not adopted on the host, or missing from libvirt) is recorded once per host and entry as a needs_attention operation (request_id adopt-attention:<host>:<kind>:<id>, actor system, error prefixed 'not adopted from host report:') with an audit entry adopt.attention naming the reason; the record is marked succeeded once the entry is adopted. A vm-create entry interrupted after its definition step is re-observed by the host on report and promoted to succeeded when the persistent domain matches its journaled definition.

token.description: Single-use pairing secret; the host presents it on POST /api/v1/agent/console/{token} within the ticket lifetime.

vm_id.description: VM UUID; omit or empty for the host console.

websocket.description: Same-origin path for the wss:// console stream; carries the ticket.

phase.description: idle, downloading, installing, restarting, done, or failed when an apply is tracked.

progress.description: Percent complete for the current apply when known.

error.description: Non-fatal repo or apply problem; installed_version remains valid for check.

after_operation_id.description: Optional earlier same-VM task which Core must find succeeded in its managed journal before effects. Never the current operation ID. Sent only to vm-power-queue-v1 hosts; persisted with the command. Core also records a local prerequisite for a new power request admitted behind pending same-VM work.

request_id.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL. Persist before sending; the same id replays the same operation.

interface.description: Guest interface name as reported by the guest agent; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

address.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address in CIDR form. Loopback and link-local addresses are omitted.

agent.description: connected: the QEMU guest agent answered; unresponsive: the org.qemu.guest_agent.0 channel is attached but the agent did not answer within 1 second; disconnected: nothing in the guest has opened the channel; no-channel: the VM definition lacks the channel.

os.description: guest-get-osinfo pretty name; absent unless agent is connected. Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

hostname.description: guest-get-host-name; absent unless agent is connected. Maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

addresses.description: guest-network-get-interfaces addresses without loopback or link-local entries; at most 32.

clipboard.description: ready: the guest opened the qemu-vdagent channel (spice-vdagent is running) so the console clipboard works both ways; waiting: the channel exists but nothing in the guest opened it; no-channel: the VM was defined before console clipboard support and must be recreated to gain it.

resize.description: True only when the guest can actually follow a console resize request: the VM has a VirtIO display and the guest has opened the qemu-vdagent channel, which is the agent that applies the new resolution. A VirtIO display alone only means the host would send the request; a guest without the driver ignores it (BUG-0201).

media.description: The live CD drive of the running VM: loaded when its tray holds media, empty when the drive holds none (a guest can eject its own disc, for example an installer after the base system), no-drive when the VM has no CD drive. Absent from Core builds that do not observe it. It reports what the guest sees; the durable media_id changes only through a media request.

drivers_media.description: The same live observation as media, for the VM's second (driver disc) CD drive. Absent from Core builds that define only one CD drive.

GuestInfo.description: Observed inside a running VM by its host through host-local virtio channels: guest agent facts and console channel states. Observation only; a connected agent is not proof of application health.

drive.description: Which of the VM's two CD drives the request applies to: install (or omitted, which is what every Controller sent before the second drive existed) or drivers. Core resolves the drive through libvirt user aliases, so the target letters libvirt assigns never matter. A Controller must not send drivers to a host that does not report vm-media-drivers-drive-v1.

media_id.description: ISO media ID already imported on the assigned host. Required for insert; omitted for eject.

id.description: Lowercase libvirt domain UUID of the appliance VM.

request_id.description: The deployment's stable request ID, which is also the request_id of POST /api/v1/appliances/adopt during the handoff.

Appliance.description: A Controller appliance VM the host deployed through its local appliance engine and still owns, reported from that engine's deploy journal (the host's durable ownership record).

operation_id.description: The host journal's operation ID: the Controller operation ID when this Controller issued it; <operation-id>:start for the automatic start of a vm-create entry.

id.description: Resource ID the operation addressed (registration, media or VM ID).

ManagedOutcome.description: Host-owned queued work and retained task outcomes. A replacement Controller adopts these passively, follows terminal status, and never redispatches them. Core retains admission order through restart and reenrollment.

id.description: Omit, or the VM UUID from the path.

pool_id.description: Must equal the VM's pool; editing never moves a VM.

host_id.description: Must equal the VM's assigned host; editing never moves a VM.

name.description: Nonblank VM name, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (the byte limit is additionally enforced by Controller and Core). Spaces, case, dots, punctuation and Unicode are preserved exactly. Slashes, control characters and XML-invalid U+FFFE/U+FFFF are rejected. Core checks uniqueness on the host, journals the name and reports it for Controller adoption; failed or uncertain creations retain their reservation. Upgrade Controller and Core together to use the expanded naming syntax.

description.description: Free-text operator note, at most 4096 characters.

guest_os.description: Guest OS hint recorded for display and guest-tools advice; empty leaves it unset. It installs nothing and does not change the VM devices: disk bus and NIC model are chosen per device.

disks.description: One to eight disks; names unique within the VM.

media_id.description: Install ISO (Media.id), empty for none. The ISO must be imported and verified on the placement host; it may live on any storage that host can read and does not need to share a repository with the VM's disks. Every VM has the CD drive, so a non-zero boot.media_boot_order does not require media_id: an emptied drive keeps its place in the boot order.

start_after_create.description: Must be false; use the power controls to start a VM.

autostart.description: libvirt autostart, set while the stopped guest is defined so the host starts this VM on boot. It is not a start.

UpdateVMRequest.description: The complete desired definition of an existing VM plus a stable request_id. Disks are matched to the current definition by name (storage, size and provisioning of an existing disk cannot change); interfaces by MAC, so send existing interfaces with the address the VM list reports and leave mac empty only for new ones. Controller answers 400 when an interface at an existing index has an empty mac and the request removes an interface or that interface's network, model or MTU differs from the current interface at that index; an unchanged interface or one appended past the current count may still omit it. Changing an existing interface's MAC is treated as removing that interface and adding a new one, which a running VM accepts.

request_id.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL. Persist before sending; the same id replays the same operation.

delete_disks.description: When true, Core unlinks the guest disk files after undefine. When false (default), files stay on storage and are recorded as retained.

VMTombstone.description: Intentional vm-delete tombstone from Core so Controller drops its mirror. Not the same as missing_vms.

token.description: Stats channel secret for this host; the host presents it on POST /api/v1/agent/stats/{token}.

StatsTier.description: Not serialized. Range-to-resolution table shared by Core and Controller: 10m = 5 s × 120, 24h = 1 min × 1440, 30d = 1 h × 720, 1y = 1 day × 365.

key.description: Stable series key, e.g. cpu.total, cpu.vcpu.0, cpu.core.3, memory.assigned, memory.host, memory.guest_used, memory.used, memory.total, disk.vda.read_bytes, disk.vda.write_iops, net.0.rx, net.eno1.tx, load.1. Keys ending .total are aggregates.

values.description: One entry per step from start; null is unknown or not running, never zero. Exactly the range's point count (live and 10m 120, 24h 1440, 30d 720, 1y 365); the Controller relay answers 502 for a reply with any other length.

host_id.description: Host that holds this history; set by the Controller relay.

start.description: Time of values[0], aligned to a step boundary.

StatsHistory.description: Usage history kept on the host in fixed-size round-robin files under the agent state directory. The Controller keeps no copy.

GET /appliance-ready.json.description: Appliance-only public JSON file served by the existing Controller UI file handler, not a separately registered API route. First boot atomically publishes it after initialization, verified local HTTPS UI HTTP 200, and guest bootstrap-secret cleanup. It must be absent from a pristine appliance image and may return 404 before preparation or on non-appliance deployments. A persisted marker records first-boot completion; it is not continuous health or successful host enrollment/adoption.
GET /appliance-ready.json.compatibility: Host handoff requires bootstrap_version 1, status ready and a successful UI root response over the pinned Controller TLS identity. An older API-only Controller cannot satisfy appliance readiness.

refresh-inventory.payload: None: only operation_id and kind. Created by POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/operations with a stable request_id; at most one queued or dispatched refresh per host.
refresh-inventory.semantics: Read-only request for a fresh host inventory sample. Core journals it as pending without a managed payload and completes it succeeded when a probe inventory observed after admission is reported, or failed with 'fresh host inventory unavailable before probe deadline'. A pending refresh restarts its deadline after agent restart so it reconciles against a new sample. Delivered without the managed capability. A repeated operation_id is ignored as already admitted, including for legacy journal entries without a stored command; no effects are repeated.

pool-member-join.semantics: Reserved master-directed pool command. Core refuses it because membership is admitted only through the authenticated one-use Core-peer exchange; Controller cannot create or replace membership.

pool-storage-reconcile.semantics: Master-directed reconciliation for one NFS or SMB repository. The addressed member pulls the master record over pinned TLS 1.3 peer mTLS, stores an SMB secret only in its own Core credential state, journals native preparation, verifies QEMU access and a cross-Core non-blocking lock, then posts its generation-bound access observation. Before member VM/media work it reserves the current repository generation at the master; failed local work releases that reservation, while a durable definition retains it until the healthy serialized member journal proves it unused. Master source/credential/detach mutations write a Core-owned marker and fail closed while reservations exist. Local ZFS, ordinary iSCSI and generic native disks remain local and are refused/no fencing applies. Controller does not authorize membership, receive SMB secret bytes, or drive retries.

peer_lock.security: Pinned TLS 1.3 mTLS; current authenticated pool member. POST checks repository eligibility and generation. Lease ownership is bound to the authenticated member, repository, generation, challenge and mode.

parameters.challenge: 32 hexadecimal characters, generated randomly per attempt
parameters.probe_mode: Optional challenge-byte-v1; absent means legacy byte zero

peer_lock.acknowledgement: 204; challenge-byte-v1 POST echoes X-Nex-Pool-Probe-Mode: challenge-byte-v1. Missing echo selects legacy byte zero; a different nonempty echo fails closed.
peer_lock.semantics: A nonzero one-byte OFD range derived from the challenge on .nex-peer-lock isolates simultaneous proofs. Only EAGAIN/EACCES establish conflict; after DELETE the member must acquire the same range. A rare range collision fails closed. Unknown modes and malformed challenges are rejected; unavailable generation or lock returns failure. Leases expire after ten seconds and are not VM ownership or fencing authority.
peer_lock.compatibility: New master supports legacy byte-zero requests. New member falls back to byte zero when an old master omits the acknowledgement, retaining the legacy contention limitation. Core retries periodically with a fresh challenge; no Controller retry job or new durable state.
peer_lock.offset: SHA-256 of decoded 16-byte challenge; big-endian uint64 of first eight digest bytes, AND ((1<<63)-2), then add one. Byte zero is reserved for legacy peers.

lease_limit.at_capacity: New leases return lock-unavailable conflict; exact held-lease replay remains idempotent. Release or ten-second expiry frees capacity.

storage-register.semantics: Verify existing local directory access; no formatting. Refuse, as a failed result, a path another non-failed registration on this host already holds. The host self-registers /var/lib/libvirt/images as ISO through this same verification, with a host-generated ID, unless any journal entry already holds that path. Succeeded registrations are reported back in Inventory.managed.storage and adopted by a Controller that does not hold them (request_id adopt-storage:<host>:<id>) without redelivery.

storage-update.semantics: A name-only update is metadata-only and preserves credentials without reconnecting. Source changes and credential rotation are guarded: rotation requires all referring VMs shut off and no pending or needs_attention disk/media/ISO work. Core compares generation, journals intent before effects, reports needs_attention if rollback is uncertain, and never returns or journals credential bytes.

storage-recheck.semantics: Core observes the registered source without changing configuration or credentials. A missing, replaced, readonly or inaccessible backing source is reported and blocks future disk/media writes; it never uses an empty mountpoint. An identical Controller replay only returns the original operation. Core separately retries at most one due pending/needs_attention storage journal entry per minute in its serialized managed-worker lane, retaining the original result and excluding definitive failures; this continues through Controller loss.

storage-detach.semantics: Core compares expected generation and applies the full dependency guard for VM disks, retained disks, ISO media and pending/needs_attention disk or media work. A success writes a tombstone and removes only Nex-owned access configuration; it never formats, erases, destroys a zpool or target, or deletes backing files. Uncertain rollback remains needs_attention.

storage-credential-retire.semantics: Core rechecks that the opaque receipt is eligible and unreferenced before removing its local secret. A receipt already retired cannot restore or recreate a secret by replay. The command carries no credential bytes and Controller keeps no cleanup state.

network-register.semantics: Verify existing bridge or active libvirt network without edits; for kind vlan, idempotently create bridge <uplink>v<vlan> over the 802.1Q sub-interface, persist it under /etc/network/interfaces.d and refuse uplinks or VLAN devices already used by the host configuration. Refuse, as a failed result, a bridge (shared by kind bridge and vlan) or libvirt network another non-failed registration on this host already holds. The host self-registers <port> untagged for every bridge on a physical NIC or bond through this same verification, with host-generated IDs, unless any journal entry already holds that bridge. Succeeded registrations are reported back in Inventory.managed.networks and adopted by a Controller that does not hold them (request_id adopt-network:<host>:<id>) without redelivery.

iso-import.semantics: Without media.url, fetch assigned staged media over host mTLS and verify supplied size/hash/ISO. With media.url, require iso-download-v1 and zero initial size/hash; Core downloads public HTTP(S) destinations with DNS/redirect address checks, no credentials or environment proxies, capacity limits and ISO validation. Core records computed size/hash in its durable applied journal, then reports Inventory.managed.media without URL. Controller mirrors completion metadata and a fresh Controller re-adopts identities and names. Interrupted dispatched work is reconciled through the journal; ambiguous imports require attention.

vm-create.semantics: Create a stopped VM from the full specification: one exclusive new qcow2 per disk inside the VM's own directory on each disk's storage target (sparse when thin, preallocated when not), one interface per NIC with its derived or manual MAC, per-device boot order, the memory mode's balloon and physical-backing configuration, the selected firmware and machine type, and libvirt autostart when requested. Refuse, as a failed result, a name another domain or non-failed journal entry on this host holds, an effective MAC (manual or derived) any domain or journal entry holds, and dedicated memory that, with what is already promised plus the 2 GiB host reserve, exceeds total host memory. When start_after_create is set, start the guest once after the definition is verified and record the outcome in the entry's start field; the creation result is succeeded either way. A retry or reconciliation never starts twice: an interruption at the start step is reconciled by observing libvirt (running means started, otherwise the start outcome reads 'interrupted before the automatic start completed'). A failed start keeps the VM defined and stopped and is reported as a separate outcome <operation-id>:start of kind vm-power, status failed, error 'VM created but not started: <reason>'. Reconcile journal and per-disk ownership on replay. Core resolves storage, network and media references by resource ID, not by pool/host ID, so creation works after re-enrollment under a new Controller. Succeeded definitions are reported back in Inventory.managed.vms and adopted by a Controller that does not hold them (request_id adopt-vm:<host>:<id>) without redelivery.

vm-power.semantics: Issue one libvirt start/shutdown/reboot/destroy/reset for the named VM on this host. start and force-stop are idempotent against the observed state; shutdown and reboot are ACPI requests the guest may ignore; force-reboot maps to virsh reset, is running-only, and shares reboot's interrupt ambiguity; paused or transitional states are refused. The stage is journaled before the single request so an interruption is reconciled by observation only: succeeded when the observed state proves the outcome, otherwise needs_attention; never a second request. Queue-capable hosts (vm-power-queue-v1) persist FIFO command admission and check after_operation_id is a successful same-VM task before effects; no retry loop for genuine failures. Host-received queued commands survive restart/replacement and are reported as managed outcomes for passive adoption. Shutdown/reboot completion remains ACPI acceptance, not proof of guest shutdown.

vm-delete.semantics: Undefine a stopped managed VM. Requires observed shut off. delete_disks=false retains qcow2 paths in the journal; delete_disks=true unlinks them after undefine. UEFI guests use virsh undefine --nvram. Succeeded deletes omit the VM from Applied.vms and emit DeletedVMs tombstones for Controller mirror removal. An interrupted undefine or wipe resumes when the same operation is delivered again: a domain still defined must be shut off (otherwise needs_attention 'stop the VM so its interrupted delete can finish; observed state is <state>'), undefine repeats with the same flags and a requested wipe repeats over the journaled paths, ignoring files already gone. A later vm-delete for the same VM settles the interrupted one only when delete_disks matches and then fails as already deleted; a different delete_disks choice is refused. Disks of a VM deleted with delete_disks=true no longer count as storage-detach dependencies.

vm-media.semantics: Insert a verified ISO into, or eject media from, the named VM's CD drive on this host with one libvirt change-media (live and persistent). Insert attaches an empty CD drive first when the domain has none; eject on a drive that is already empty (checked against the live definition of a running VM) succeeds without any libvirt call and never attaches a drive. The resolved media path and the changing-media stage are journaled in one write immediately before the change, so an interruption before that write is simply re-applied and one after it is reconciled by observing the domain: succeeded when the drive holds the requested media (or none, for eject), otherwise needs_attention. Core records only media_id in the VM's journaled specification; boot order values are never rewritten because change-media leaves every device's bootindex as it is.

vm-update.semantics: Apply one revision of an existing VM's definition; refuse a revision other than current + 1. Classify the difference from the journal's current definition (NeedsStop): a shut-off guest is redefined after any new disks are allocated and a rename (domrename), with the same capacity, name and MAC conflict checks as creation; a running guest takes only device additions, removals and media changes, applied with attach-device/detach-device --persistent and change-media --live --config, and is refused before any effect for anything else; an added interface whose MAC is still live after an earlier removal the guest has not released is refused and the task fails before any effect. Disks are matched by name and keep their journaled target names; interfaces by MAC. Removed disk files are retained and listed in the journal. The persistent definition and per-disk ownership are then observed against the regenerated XML by device identity; an interruption is reconciled by observation, except a UEFI-to-BIOS change interrupted after its undefine (stage cleaning-nvram or defining), which Core finishes by confirming the domain is absent and defining the journaled BIOS XML, and which refuses to undefine a UEFI domain that reappeared. A stopped edit that renames the VM and changes Secure Boot runs the read-only Secure Boot checks first, then domrename, then the variable-store edit and define. The journal reports the highest succeeded revision as the VM's current definition.
